root_cause.text: The fsl_spi_prepare_message function in the spi-fsl-cpm driver omitted a length parity check before switching to 16-bit mode, causing a buffer overrun when odd-length transfers are processed in 16-bit mode.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `!(t->len & 1)` to the condition that enables 16-bit mode: `if (t->bits_per_word == 8 && t->len >= 256 && !(t->len & 1) && (mpc8xxx_spi->flags & SPI_CPM1))`. The commit message states: "Add the missing length parity verification and remain in 8 bit mode when the length is not even." The CVE description notes that commit fc96ec826bce "failed to make sure that the size is really even before switching to 16 bit mode" and that this causes a buffer overrun when an odd-length transfer occurs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix bug where odd-length transfers >=256 bytes in CPM1 mode could be incorrectly converted to 16-bit word size, causing incomplete data transfer.
intent_record.what: Added condition `!(t->len & 1)` to the if-statement that sets bits_per_word to 16 for CPM1 mode transfers with 8-bit words and length >= 256.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that the transfer length is even before converting to 16-bit word mode, preventing potential misalignment or incomplete transfer of the last byte when the length is odd.
